newsitem.title: SHARJAH: CRICKET-MOIN BATS PAKISTAN OUT OF TROUBLE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MOIN BATS PAKISTAN OUT OF TROUBLE.

text.p: Wicketkeeper Moin Khan hit a match-winning 61 to rescue Pakistan when they looked headed for certain defeat against Zimbabwe in the Sharjah Cup tournament on Wednesday.
Going to the crease with Pakistan on 41 for five, which rapidly became 51 for seven, Moin smashed 61 from 97 balls with three fours and a six to post his highest score in 75 one-day internationals.

He enabled Pakistan to recover to a still vulnerable 151 for nine in their 50 overs but then their spin twins Mushtaq Ahmed and Saqlain Mushtaq took six wickets between them to dismiss Zimbabwe for 119 in 40.1 overs.
The win ensured Pakistan's place in the final against World Cup champions Sri Lanka on Friday.
Moin and Saqlain Mushtaq (20) put on 77 runs for the eighth wicket as Pakistan staged a recovery.
Fast bowler Heath Streak was the most successful Zimbabwe bowler with the remarkable figures of four for 18 from his 10 overs.

Fast bowler Waqar Younis quickly made inroads into the Zimbabwe batting by dismissing both openers with only 14 on the board before leg-spinner Mushtaq Ahmed and off-spinner Saqlain Mushtaq took control.
Andy Flower (28) and Paul Strang (26) fleetingly gave Zimbabwe hope as they took the total to 57 for two but then the last eight wickets fell in the space of 62 runs.
Mushtaq Ahmed took four for 27, Younis three for 14 and Saqlain Mushtaq two for 37.
